title: Cross-team dependency commitment contracts and health index
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Summary:
We need a lightweight, machine-readable "dependency commitment" artifact and a corresponding Dependency Health Index (DHI) to accelerate roadmap alignment across Eng/Design/Security/Infra and to create objective signals for go/no-go gating. The goal is to reduce late-stage surprises by making ownership, acceptance criteria, minimal viable integrations, and blocker windows explicit and machine-queryable.
background_and_rationale:
Context:
Recent cross-team launches (Dedicated capacity autoscaler, Private upgrade flow) surfaced surprise blockers from infra schema changes and security signoffs. Current dependency trackers are free-text and manual; PMs and Eng leads spend significant time in status syncs. A compact contract + health index will enable: 1) auto-escalation for blocked critical paths; 2) automated roadmap risk dashboards; 3) consistent handoff artifacts for design and verification teams.
proposal:
Deliverables:
- Dependency Commitment Template (YAML + UI form) capturing: owner, minimal acceptance criteria, required APIs, expected delivery window, SLAs for review/response, and fallback/rescue plan.
- Dependency Health Index (numeric 0-100) computed from: owner availability, pass/fail of acceptance tests, integration readiness, security/compliance signoff status, and contingency readiness.
- Console integration: per-initiative dependency card with current DHI, last update, and one-click escalate.
- Weekly automated alerts for DHI < 60 for P0/P1 initiatives.
- Exportable artifacts for post-mortems and retro analysis.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives:
Options considered:
- Heavyweight contract with legal signoff: rejected due to friction for fast-moving infra and design work.
- Purely human-run dependency huddles: lowest engineering cost but scales poorly and provides no machine signals.
- Minimal triage-only fields in existing tracker: too little structure to compute an index or automate escalations.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (MVP, 6 weeks): YAML contract spec + PM/Eng UI prototype, DHI v1 calculation (owner set, acceptance checkbox, signoff flags), manual webhook to PagerDuty for DHI < 50 escalations.
Phase 1 (next 6 weeks): integrate with Console initiative pages, add automated DHI computation from CI test results and security ticket status, enable in 3 pilot initiatives.
Phase 2 (Q1 rollout): set alerts in org-wide roadmap dashboard, add canary auto-escalation policies, and run month-long training clinics for PMs and Eng leads.
acceptance_criteria: A YAML dependency contract can be created or edited from the Console initiative page
DHI v1 is computed and visible on initiative dependency cards
Automated PagerDuty webhook triggers for DHI < 50 for P0 initiatives
At least three pilot initiatives (one Eng-led, one Design-heavy, one Security-dependent) adopt the contract and show reduced ad-hoc syncs in two sprints
A migration guide exists to convert current free-text dependencies into the structured contract
metrics: Baseline: average number of cross-team blocking syncs per initiative (last 6 months): 3.2
Target: reduce blocking syncs by 50% for pilot initiatives within two cycles
DHI adoption: 100% for pilot initiative dependencies
Escalation accuracy: <15% false positives for PagerDuty alerts
